title: Separation techniques of mixture
competency: Separate mixtures using differences in size, magnetism, density, solubility and boiling point.

Separating particles of different sizes with a sieve.

ideas.name: Separation by hand, sieving and magnets

en.text: Mixtures can be separated by physical methods that use differences in their properties. Large pieces can be picked out by hand or held back by a sieve. A magnet pulls iron filings out of sand, because iron is magnetic and sand is not.

screens.title: Teff and peas
screens.ask: Your mother has teff mixed with a few peas. What is the easiest way to separate them?
opts: Pick the peas out by hand or use a sieve
screens.after: Peas are much bigger than teff grains. Pick them out, or let the teff pass through a sieve.

screens.title: 2.5.1 Separation techniques of mixture
paras: Most substances around us are mixtures.
Mixtures can be separated into pure substances.
Separating parts of a mixture by physical methods is a separation process.
Methods use differences in size, magnetism, melting point, boiling point and solubility.
Methods include separation by hand, sieving, filtration, evaporation, magnetic separation, decantation and distillation.

screens.title: I. Magnetic separation
paras: Magnetic separation separates magnetic and non-magnetic substances.
Sand mixed with iron filings is a heterogeneous mixture.
A magnet attracts the iron filings but not the sand.

screens.title: Experiment 2.4 Separation using a bar magnet
steps: Mix the sand with the iron filings on a plate.
Wrap a plastic bag around the bar magnet.
Hold the magnet over the plate. The iron collects on the magnet.
Remove the bag carefully and scrape off the iron filings.
The sand stays on the plate.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Separation process
Separating the parts of a mixture by physical methods, using differences in their physical properties.
Magnetic separation
Using a magnet to separate magnetic from non-magnetic substances.
Sieving
Separating particles of different sizes with a sieve.

screens.text: Why is the sand not attracted by the magnet?
screens.why: Only magnetic substances such as iron are attracted.
screens.clue: What makes iron different from sand?

screens.text: How would you separate iron and charcoal?
screens.why: Iron is attracted by a magnet; charcoal is not.

screens.text: A sieve with 2 mm holes is shaken over soil. What is separated, and by which property?
opts: Larger particles from fine earth, by size
Salt from water, by boiling point
screens.ans: Larger particles from fine earth, by size
screens.why: Fine earth passes through the 2 mm holes; larger particles stay. Sieving uses differences in particle size.
screens.clue: What decides whether a grain falls through?

en.text: Decantation separates a liquid from a settled solid, or from another liquid that does not mix, by pouring off the top layer. Clear coffee is poured from the jebena this way. Immiscible liquids like oil and water, or kerosene and water, are separated with a separating funnel: the heavier liquid runs out at the bottom.

screens.title: Jebena coffee
screens.ask: Coffee grounds sink to the bottom of the jebena. How do we get a clear cup of coffee?
opts: Pour slowly and leave the grounds behind
screens.after: Pouring off the clear liquid above the settled grounds is decantation.

screens.title: II. Decantation
paras: Decantation separates a liquid from a solid, or from an immiscible liquid.
You pour off the top liquid layer and leave the layer below.
Cooking oil and water form two layers: water at the bottom, oil on top.
Pour the oil into another vessel. The water stays behind.

screens.title: Separating funnel
paras: Liquids that do not mix form two layers. They are immiscible liquids.
A separating funnel is a glass funnel with a tap (stop-cock) in its stem.
The heavier liquid forms the lower layer; the lighter one is on top.
Open the tap to run the lower layer into a beaker. Then collect the upper layer.
Kerosene and water, and oil and water, are separated this way.

screens.caption: A funnel; a separating funnel also has a tap in its stem.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Decantation
Pouring off the top liquid layer from a solid or another liquid below.
Separating funnel
A glass funnel with a tap, used to separate immiscible liquids.
Immiscible liquids
Liquids that do not mix and form layers, like oil and water.

screens.text: Immiscible liquids can be separated by using a …
screens.why: The tap lets the lower layer run out first.

screens.text: In a separating funnel with kerosene and water, which layer runs out first through the tap?
screens.why: The heavier liquid is at the bottom, next to the tap.
screens.clue: Which liquid is at the bottom?

screens.text: Muddy water is left to stand, then the clear water is poured off. Which two steps are used?
screens.why: First the mud settles (sedimentation). Then the clear water is poured off (decantation).

en.text: Filtration removes an insoluble solid from a liquid. The liquid passes through filter paper as the filtrate; the solid stays as the residue. Evaporation separates a dissolved solid from its liquid: heating drives off the liquid and the solid stays, as when salt is recovered from salt water.

screens.title: Get the salt back
screens.ask: You dissolve salt in water. How can you get the salt back?
screens.after: Salt passes through filter paper, because it is dissolved. Evaporating the water leaves the salt.

screens.title: III. Filtration
paras: Filtration removes insoluble solids from a liquid using filter paper.
Filter paper has tiny pores that let only liquids through.
The liquid that passes through is the filtrate.
The solid left on the paper is the residue.
Chalk and water, soil and water are separated this way. Filtration helps purify tap water.

screens.title: IV. Evaporation
paras: Evaporation separates a soluble solid from a liquid.
The liquid (solvent) is vaporized and the solid (solute) is left.
We separate salt from salt solution by evaporating the water.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Filtration
Removing an insoluble solid from a liquid with filter paper.
Filtrate
The liquid that passes through the filter paper.
Residue
The solid left behind on the filter paper.
Evaporation
Heating a solution so the liquid escapes and the dissolved solid stays.

screens.text: Dirty water is poured into a funnel lined with paper. Clean water comes out; dirt stays on the paper. This is …
screens.why: The water is the filtrate; the dirt is the residue.
Pick the method that uses the right difference in properties.
screens.clue: Is the solid dissolved or not?

screens.ask: In filtration, the solid left on the filter paper is called the ___.
screens.why: The liquid is the filtrate; the solid is the residue.

screens.text: A mixture of salt and sand must be separated. Which order works?
opts: Dissolve in water, filter, then evaporate the filtrate
screens.ans: Dissolve in water, filter, then evaporate the filtrate
screens.why: Salt dissolves, sand does not. Filtering removes the sand. Evaporating the filtrate leaves the salt.

en.text: Distillation boils a liquid and condenses its vapour in a cooled tube to collect it. It gives pure water from salt water. It also separates miscible liquids with very different boiling points: ethanol boils at 78 °C and water at 100 °C, so the alcohol vaporizes first and is collected as the distillate.

screens.title: Which boils first?
screens.ask: Ethanol boils at 78 °C and water at 100 °C. A mixture of them is heated slowly. Which boils off first?
screens.after: Ethanol has the lower boiling point, so it vaporizes first.

screens.title: V. Distillation
paras: Distillation is boiling a liquid into vapour, then condensing the vapour back to a liquid.
It is used to get pure water from salt solution.
The mixture is heated. The most volatile part vaporizes first.
The vapour passes through a cooled tube, the condenser, and becomes liquid.
The liquid collected is the distillate.

screens.title: Figure 2.23 Simple distillation set-up
items: Shows the temperature of the vapour.
A tube cooled by running water. Vapour turns back to liquid.

screens.title: Miscible liquids
paras: Liquids that mix to form a solution are miscible liquids.
Alcohol and water are miscible.
Ethanol boils at 78 °C; water boils at 100 °C.
On heating, the alcohol vaporizes faster and is collected as distillate.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Distillation
Boiling a liquid and condensing its vapour to collect it.
Distillate
The liquid collected after condensing in distillation.
Miscible liquids
Liquids that mix to form a solution, like alcohol and water.

screens.text: How would you separate a mixture of alcohol and water?
screens.why: They are miscible liquids with different boiling points.
screens.clue: They mix, so a funnel will not work.

screens.text: In distillation, the condenser cools the vapour so it turns back into a liquid.
screens.why: Cool water runs around the condenser tube.

screens.text: Which separation method collects BOTH the salt and the pure water from salt water?
screens.why: In distillation the water vapour is condensed and collected; the salt stays in the flask. Open evaporation loses the water to the air.
screens.clue: In which method is the vapour caught?

items.title: Q1 A–D: choose a method
pairs: B. Iron filings and sulfur powder
items.why: Use size, magnetism, solubility and layers.
items.clue: What is different about the two parts?

items.title: Q1 E–H: choose a method

items.text: i. Mixture of salt, sand and water:
opts: Filter off the sand, then evaporate the filtrate
items.ans: Filter off the sand, then evaporate the filtrate
items.why: Sand is the residue; salt stays in the filtrate until evaporated.

items.text: ii. Mixture of common salt, iron filings and sand:
opts: Magnet first, then dissolve, filter and evaporate
items.ans: Magnet first, then dissolve, filter and evaporate
items.why: Remove iron while dry; then separate salt from sand.

items.text: iii. Mixture of oil, water and sand:
opts: Filter off the sand, then use a separating funnel
items.ans: Filter off the sand, then use a separating funnel
items.why: Sand is insoluble; oil and water form layers.

opts: Dissolve, filter off the clay, gently evaporate
items.ans: Dissolve, filter off the clay, gently evaporate

test.text: Which method separates iron filings from sand?

test.ask: The liquid that passes through filter paper is called the ___.
test.why: The solid left behind is the residue.

test.text: A mixture of sand and sugar can be separated by …
opts: dissolution followed by filtration and evaporation
dissolution followed by evaporation and filtration
test.ans: dissolution followed by filtration and evaporation
test.why: Dissolve the sugar, filter off the sand, evaporate to get the sugar.

test.text: Kerosene and water are best separated using a …
Iron filings, sand and salt must be separated. Which order is most appropriate?
test.why: Magnet first while dry, then dissolve the salt, filter off sand, evaporate.
